title: Avoiding finitely many homogeneous primes by a homogeneous element of positive degree
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a graded ideal I contained in the positive-degree part and not contained in any of finitely many homogeneous primes contains a homogeneous element of positive degree avoiding all of them (statement lines 13846-13853). The proof does not reduce to the general prime avoidance lemma: it inducts on the number of primes, and in the critical case where the previously chosen homogeneous element lies in the last prime it uses that I times the product of the other primes is not contained in the last prime, takes a homogeneous witness, and combines the two witnesses as x to the degree of y plus y to the degree of x (proof lines 13855-13865). That swap of exponents is the step that makes the result homogeneous, and the author displays it. H2.
